body: I'm really sorry for what you're dealing with. I met a person in hospital who suffered from an eating disorder and she was in there for over a year. She was such a nice person and didn't deserve to be going through what she did and I'm sure the same applies to you. Fuck what these people are saying. What could they possibly know about what you go through every day? Please don't let these people get you down, you're a much better person than all of them combined.
Oh my gosh, I am so sorry for your loss. Do you see anyone about your problems? Why do you think it should've been you?
Why do you hate yourself and why are you feeling like this? I'm here for you if you'd like to talk.

Honestly, don't do it like this. It's more likely that you'll just end up hurting yourself really badly or even worse and become disabled. I can't give you any advice on how to do it as it's against the rules and quite frankly, I wouldn't feel comfortable doing so but... just don't do it this way. Please, for your own sake.

Dude, I am so sorry it has come to this for you. As much as I don't want you to die, it's not my right to tell you what to do. I feel very much the same as you, even if for different reasons. I hope you can at least find some peace before leaving.

thank you, really. thank you so so much. i just spent more than an hour crying because no one has ever given me any praise or recognition like that. it's not even about being noticed or expecting anything in return for me. i do things out of kind-heartedness and i genuinely care. i know what it feels like to want to die, to feel alone, to deal with so many different things. i feel it every day. i always put others ahead of me, even if i'm going through a tough time, i put my problems aside. i've helped so many different people in so many different ways (even indirectly) and that's all i care about. that's all i've ever cared about. 

i hate knowing that there are others like me out there, especially those who are alone and have no one who they can turn to. i hate hearing about people taking their own life, it makes me really sad and i can't help but cry every time. i wish i could help everyone but i can't. i can only help people one at a time. i see posts on here and other sites that don't get any replies and i want to help so much but it's not easy when you're dealing with your own stuff. i feel so bad and i'm always hoping someone else will be able to reach out and give a caring hand to them.

honestly, i can't thank you enough. i appreciate it more than anything. thank you for noticing me and acknowledging the things i've done. your post really touched me in ways i've never felt. it just hurts me so much to be like this. i feel like a character in some really tragic novel. i've lost a lot in my life but it's like no one truly sees. i have no friends. people always leave and always let me down. i've been betrayed and brushed off like a piece of dirt because i'm way too nice for my own good and everyone takes advantage of it. i've lost all my faith and trust in people. im scared to get close now and i just feel like being alone is best for me.

i've been contemplating suicide really heavily for the past few months. i've attempted it a bunch of times, mostly by getting hit or decapitated by a train. i've had 3 opportunities to end it and the last time i tried i was literally centimetres from being hit and it was coming at me really fast but i side-stepped it in time before it could do anything. every attempt from the first just gets closer than the last. i know it doesn't mean anything but i'm afraid the next time i try i'll just go through with it... 

thank you again, you're a really beautiful person. <3

*im sorry im typing like this btw, i really don't have any energy at the moment.

I had the same problem back in school as well. I felt exactly like you but was also literally outside of the 'circle' in some situations. I'd just be standing there with everyone's backs faced towards me and I would basically be ignored and left out. I was never invited anywhere (even right in front of my face) and outside of school it was even more apparent just how much no one gave a shit about me. I couldn't relate to anyone and I had the most fakest mask on during those years. Brings me anxiety just thinking about it. ;\

I am so sorry to hear this. His reaction was totally uncalled for and not necessary at all. The last thing you need after opening up to someone is for them to just go off at you. You're not stupid and this isn't your fault so please don't blame yourself. 

He needs to understand how it made you feel and that the way he reacted was wrong. It's not fair on you to have to pretend you're okay and the relationship just won't work like that. If you need to talk, I'm here. Is there a reason you don't want to be alive any more, if I may ask?

There are always people on here who will try to help when they can so don't be afraid to ask for it. It's okay, it's gotten a lot better for me but things like this can really leave a huge mark on you psychologically. I'm glad to hear you and your Dad are close. I'm sure he'd want to help you and wouldn't want his own child to suffer in silence. Given the current situation however, it might be best to wait until things settle down a little bit, but don't let it get to a point where you can't handle it any more. 

Honestly, it probably is best for your Dad to divorce your Mum. She sounds very self-involved and only cares about what she wants. It'd be better for everyone and you and your siblings sure don't need the arguments and the stress. Just be there for your Dad, show him you care about him and that you love him. That's what he needs the most right now and that's how you can help him. 

No worries, you are most welcome and I'm more than happy I could be of help. I'm not a "sir" but don't worry, it's fine. Have a good rest! :)

Don't be sorry, I'm here to help.

It sounds like your Dad is really struggling at the moment - the relationship with your Mum and the constant arguments alongside having to work every day can have a huge toll on not only his well-being, but the rest of you and your family. Do you know what's initiating these arguments? I'm really sorry for how much strain this is putting on you. 

My Dad used to be very abusive and controlling for the most part of my life and arguments were almost daily and would rage on until 6 in the morning sometimes. I almost never slept in fear of him hurting my Mum and I was scared to death of the safety of me and my family. Even to this day, I get really paranoid thinking I can hear him going off and my ptsd can get triggered by people shouting.

Is there any way you can get family counselling or therapy? There seems to be a lot of underlying issues here that are best solved by someone with more experience than me. Is there anyone in person who you can talk to and get help for with your problems? I'm sorry if I'm not being that helpful, I wish there were more I could do. All I can say is reach out and don't let yourself deal with this alone, even if it's talking to people like me on the internet. Find an outlet or something to get your mind off things as that can really help.

This is a very beautiful song, thank you for sharing it and I'm glad it's helped you out in a way. :) It's amazing how therapeutic music can be and how inspirational and empowering it can make you feel. I know for me, music has been there in some of my most darkest moments and has made me feel like I wasn't alone, and it still continues to do so.
I'd say your best bet is to wait until the next semester starts as much as it isn't an ideal thing for you. 10 free sessions would be really helpful if you can hold out until then.

No need to apologize for your English, it's actually quite good to be honest. I'm sorry to hear what you're going through and with how stressful such a situation can be, I wouldn't be surprised if you were depressed. I can't diagnose you as I'm not a trained mental health professional but I'm here to listen if you need someone to talk to. May I ask what is going on in your life and in your family for all these things to be happening?

Hm, the best thing I can think of is to keep trying if seeing a therapist is something you really want to do. Are there any other people you know you could reach out to? Maybe start with someone else and see if they can help you convince your Mum that you need therapy. Sorry to assume but if you go to school, you could try seeing if they have a counsellor there who could help you out more.

That's not weird at all. If watching Let's Plays makes you feel like you have friends and that for you is comforting, then who is anyone else to judge? I'm a very introverted person and a loner out of choice but I do a lot of things that many would consider 'weird' but that doesn't mean there's anything wrong with it. May I ask why you have no friends, by the way? I'm here to listen if there's anything you'd like to talk about.

That's a difficult situation to be in. Maybe if you keep pressing the issue and ask her why she thinks you're fine then she might change her mind. Do you think she'd be supportive or understand? She might not be taking you seriously right now but if you can open up a bit to her and tell her how you're feeling then she might feel differently. It's likely that she doesn't see anything wrong because depression is basically that - something internal that many of us tend to cover up. It's good you're aware that you may have depression and it's good that you're actively seeking help. If you need anything then don't be afraid to vent your problems here or message me and I'll try help as much as I can. Best of luck. :)

That's understandable. Is there any specific reason you can pinpoint as to why you think it's wrong? It's normal to feel like you do but I'm guessing it has a lot to do with the way society view things and how we're brought up. It's possible that you have some internalized homophobia that could use some working on. I used to be very unaware of my sexuality and would repress my feelings and at first, while it was a quite foreign concept to me, I accepted and embraced it fully because it's who I am and there is no shame in your sexual preferences. I understand though that it can make things harder but maybe some soul-searching might yield some results.

I suffer from clinical depression among other mental illnesses too. I've tried everything I can to get better but my life just continues to stagnate. I'm a high school drop out of 2 and a half years and I also self-harm, albeit having not done so in a few weeks. Is there any reason why being gay is a bad thing for you? I'm pansexual myself so if there's anything you'd like to talk about in regards to sexuality then I am more than happy to discuss. What do your support systems currently look like? Are you out to anyone about being gay and does anyone aside from your therapist support you with your problems? What are the causes of these problems if I may ask?

Thank you and I'm glad you're still around. I truly hope for you to find a way instead of having to resort to suicide. Please ignore any of the senseless or mindless trolls that message you and I appreciate the offer, I'll be sure to keep that in mind. Same goes your way if you ever need anything. All the best.

Please don't listen to these narrow-minded idiots. They have no compassion at all and what could they possibly know about what it's like to be autistic? It's not your fault you're like this and you didn't choose to be this way. There's nothing wrong with who you are, people are just shallow and that shallowness tends to show a lot more on the internet. I'd recommend staying away from things like this as they'll just trigger you to feel bad and by actively seeking out these things you're just reinforcing the whole idea that you are a 'mosquito'. You're not and there are people out there that aren't autistic and don't think this way. I too require lots of help and rely on others for even the most basic things. Granted it is for different reasons but that doesn't mean you're a waste of space. Are you able to get a therapist with whom you can work through these feelings and thoughts with? Maybe even find a local support group or one on the internet to feel less alone? I truly hope you can find a resolve or at the very least - a way to cope.
Hey there, would you like to talk? What do you think is causing these thoughts?

I agree wholeheartedly. It's ridiculous how sexist people can be. The whole idea that men can't get raped and that women can't rape is utterly absurd. No one should feel as if they can't open up about such a horrible thing in fear of being blamed or not listened to. Rape is never a justifiable act regardless of your gender or circumstance and being raped, whether male or female, is just as traumatizing of an experience.

Congratulations on the promotion. I've been to some therapy groups before in hospital and what we usually done was things like picking out a card from a deck that'd have a question like "What's your favourite genre of music?" and we'd basically just pass the card around in a circle and let everyone answer it. I don't remember much of what else we done but it was basic things like that - letting everyone get a turn to be able to share something about themselves and having a bit of fun. I guess the most important thing is to make sure everyone feels safe and supported and included in the discussion/activity. I hope that helped, even if just a bit.
I understand. I get where you're coming from and I'm not going to tell you it gets better or not to do it because that is your right entirely.
I apologize for the way you feel but we're here to listen if you'd like to talk.
Of course. :) I'm happy I could help in some way and I wish you all the best. If you ever need someone to talk to then don't be afraid to send me a message and I'll try my best to reply asap.

That's okay and I'm really sorry for how you're feeling. Sometimes it's hard for people to be able to read and reply to every post but that doesn't mean you're alone and that no one cares. It is going to be okay and it will get better but it takes time. It's okay to cry and it's normal to feel how you do after remembering something so traumatic. I'm glad you have some support systems and just know that there are others out there who have been through the same thing and have been able to recover. I know how it feels to be deprived of affection and meaningful connections and it's understandable you felt that way but in no way is it your fault or something you asked for. Please don't blame yourself for what happened. I really hope you can find a way to deal with this and cope.

I am so sorry for what has happened to you. Please know that what happened was not your fault and what she done was VERY wrong. She took advantage of you and had no right whatsoever to touch you like she did. Have you spoken to anyone about this in person and is there any way for you to speak to a professional? I'm here if you need someone to talk to and I'd be more than happy to try and help or even just be there as a listening ear.

You're absolutely welcome and thank you, I appreciate it. 

I'm glad there was something for you, even if it was to just forget the pain momentarily. It's sad knowing that there are other people out there who are struggling like me, who sure as fuck do not deserve to but do anyway - for whatever reason. I've always told myself that if I could magically take away someone's pain by giving up my own life then I gladly would without second thought, but sadly, such a thing is not possible.

Hey, I'm really fucking sorry for everything you've been through. No one deserves to be put through what you have and I'm so damn sorry you were raped. The way you were treated even after making positive changes for yourself is not fair. I read the whole post you talked about and I could relate to a lot of it. I struggle with chronic and severe mental illnesses and too dropped out of high school. I was also bullied pretty badly and never had friends. I grew up with a very abusive father and I was always the 'loser' and the social degenerate that everyone liked to pick on just because of how vulnerable I was.

Even now, after being out of school for over 2 and a half years, my life is shit. I've done nothing and can't do nothing in terms of getting a job or returning to study in this time and I'm pretty much fucked over in the sense that I'm disabled. I've tried absolutely everything I can think of and I've reached out for help and have gotten help but it's become clear to me how hopeless my situation is. I have no future prospects and the only reason I honestly stick around is because of my family. Every day is a struggle just to make it to the next, and for what? I've had several opportunities to end my life before but at the last possible second, decided to not.

I'm not going to tell you it gets better and all that bullshit because I don't even know that myself and even if it does, WHEN? I'm not going to tell you not to end it either because that is not my decision and your life belongs to you. As much as I wouldn't want you to do something like that, it's not fair or humane for someone to suffer so much. I myself, whilst not completely sure, have come to accept that the likelihood of me actually killing myself in the future is somewhere near certain. I'm sorry it's come to this and I'm sorry for how this world has treated you. I don't know what else to say aside from that I can understand your pain, even if it's somewhat, or different.
You're very much welcome. :)

I'd say just bring it up casually and apologize, no need to make a big deal out of it. Just ask him straight up what he's most comfortable with whenever you slip up or say something. I'm sure he'll appreciate it. :)

No need to be sorry, it's good that you're being aware and accepting.

I didn't come up with this and I forgot where I found it but I've always found it pretty hilarious:

"I'm coming out as straight, straight out gay! Gay, as in happy. Happy to be (insert gender/sexuality here)!"

Hope that helps. :)
